result.builder:
Goal: one pull request that adds padLeft to strutil, documents it, and meets every line below.

Acceptance lines (all must hold at the PR head):
1. index.js exports padLeft(s, width, fill), which pads s on the left with fill (a space when fill is not given) to width characters
2. padLeft returns s unchanged when s is already width characters or longer
3. README.md has a section for every function index.js exports
4. npm test passes

Current state: index.js is an ES module (package.json has "type": "module") and exports capitalize, slugify and truncate. README.md has `## name(args)` sections for capitalize and truncate only. slugify has no section yet, so line 3 is already unmet before your change. Tests are in test/strutil.test.js and run with `node --test` through `npm test`.

Steps:
1. In index.js, add and export `padLeft(s, width, fill = ' ')` with a short doc comment like the existing ones. It returns s padded on the left with fill until it is width characters long (for example padLeft('42', 5, '0') === '00042' and padLeft('ab', 4) === '  ab'). When s.length >= width it returns s unchanged. `String.prototype.padStart` does this. Do not change the other functions.
2. In README.md, add a `## padLeft(s, width, fill)` section that says what it does, that fill defaults to a space, and that s comes back unchanged when it is already width or longer. Also add the missing `## slugify(s)` section (it returns s trimmed, in lower case, with runs of non-alphanumeric characters turned into single dashes and no dashes at the start or end). Keep the existing sections. When you are done, every function exported from index.js must have its own section.
3. In test/strutil.test.js, import padLeft and add tests for: padding with '0' ('42', 5 -> '00042'), the default space fill, s exactly width long, and s longer than width (both unchanged).
4. Run `npm test` and make sure it passes. Then list the exports in index.js and confirm that each one has a README.md section.
5. Open the pull request and link https://github.com/o/strutil/issues/7.
result.verifier:
Check out the PR head. Run every check there, one per expect line, in this order.

Check 1. Expect line: "index.js exports padLeft(s, width, fill), which pads s on the left with fill (a space when fill is not given) to width characters"
Run from the repo root: `node --input-type=module -e "import * as m from './index.js'; console.log(typeof m.padLeft, JSON.stringify(m.padLeft('42',5,'0')), JSON.stringify(m.padLeft('ab',4)), JSON.stringify(m.padLeft('x',3,'*')))"`
PASS: padLeft is an exported function, and the results are "00042", "  ab" (two spaces, then ab) and "**x". The padding is on the left, it uses fill (or a space when fill is left out), and the result is width characters long.
FAIL: padLeft is not exported or not a function, or any result differs (padding on the right, wrong length, no space when fill is left out).

Check 2. Expect line: "padLeft returns s unchanged when s is already width characters or longer"
Run: `node --input-type=module -e "import {padLeft} from './index.js'; console.log(JSON.stringify(padLeft('abc',3,'0')), JSON.stringify(padLeft('abcdef',3,'0')), JSON.stringify(padLeft('abcdef',3)))"`
PASS: the output is "abc" "abcdef" "abcdef".
FAIL: any of these strings is padded, cut or otherwise changed, or the call throws.

Check 3. Expect line: "README.md has a section for every function index.js exports"
Run: `node --input-type=module -e "import * as m from './index.js'; console.log(Object.entries(m).filter(([,v])=>typeof v==='function').map(([k])=>k).join(' '))"` to list the exported functions. Then read README.md at the head.
PASS: every function in that list (at least capitalize, slugify, truncate and padLeft) has its own section in README.md, meaning a heading that names it with text about it.
FAIL: any exported function has no section. Note: the base README has no slugify section, so look for that one in particular.

Check 4. Expect line: "npm test passes"
Run: `npm test`.
PASS: the command exits 0 with no failing tests.
FAIL: it exits non-zero or reports a failing test.

Advisory (not PASS/FAIL conditions): see whether the tests cover padLeft, including the default fill and the unchanged cases. See whether the README headings follow the existing `## name(args)` style. See whether capitalize, slugify and truncate behave as they did before.
